advances: The universal fixed-point assertion \((\mathrm{FP})\) in accepted fact `a0f438972c88d08b` is false.  An explicit product of centrally symmetric hexagonal blocks makes its best possible normalized ratio tend to zero, while the same examples have optimal normalized mixed-integer halfspace depth exactly \(1/2\) and therefore do not disprove the locked weak Oertel statement.
author: research-agent
proof:
The set \(B_b\) is the intersection of the sublevel sets of the convex functions \(|x|\) and \(2|s|+(1-b)|x|\).  It is closed and convex, is contained in \([-1,1]\times[-1/2,1/2]\), and contains a neighborhood of the origin because both defining inequalities are strict there.  Hence it is a full-dimensional convex body.  Its definition by absolute values also gives \(B_b=-B_b\).  Products preserve these properties, so every \(C_r\) is a full-dimensional centrally symmetric convex body in \(\mathbb R^{2r}\).

For one block, the only base lattice points with nonempty fibers are \(x=-1,0,1\).  At \(x=0\), the fiber is \([-1/2,1/2]\) and has length \(1\).  At each of \(x=\pm1\), the fiber is \([-b/2,b/2]\) and has length \(b\).  Therefore the product fiber at \(z\in\{-1,0,1\}^r\) is
\[
(C_r)_z
=\prod_{i=1}^r
\left[
-\frac{1-(1-b)|z_i|}{2},
\frac{1-(1-b)|z_i|}{2}
\right],
\]
so its volume is \(b^{|\operatorname{supp}z|}\).  If any \(|z_i|>1\), the fiber is empty.  Summing by support size gives
\[
T_r=\sum_{j=0}^r\binom rj2^jb^j=(1+2b)^r.
\]

Fix \(t\) and \(z_t\) satisfying all the stated feasibility conditions, and put \(\ell:=|\operatorname{supp}z_t|\).  Since \(D_{r,t}\subseteq\{-1,0,1\}^r\), its convex hull lies in \([-1,1]^r\).  Thus the lattice point \(z_t\in\operatorname{conv}(D_{r,t})\) belongs to \(\{-1,0,1\}^r\), so \(a_r(z_t)=b^\ell\).  Accepted fact `a0f438972c88d08b` proves that every \(z_t\in\mathcal C_{r,t}\) has \(a_r(z_t)>t\).  Together with feasibility and \(b<\theta _0\), this yields
\[
b^{\ell+1}<\theta _0b^\ell\leq t<b^\ell.
\]
It follows exactly that
\[
D_{r,t}=\{z\in\{-1,0,1\}^r:|\operatorname{supp}z|\leq\ell\}.
\]
Indeed, every point of support at most \(\ell\) has mass at least \(b^\ell>t\), whereas every point of support at least \(\ell+1\) has mass at most \(b^{\ell+1}<t\).  Summing \(a_r(z)-t\) over the \(2^j\binom rj\) points of support \(j\) proves the displayed exact formula for \(W_r(t)\).

We next expose \(z_t\) inside \(D_{r,t}\).  If \(\ell\geq1\), define the proper closed halfspace
\[
J_t:=\left\{x\in\mathbb R^r:
\sum_{i\in\operatorname{supp}z_t}(z_t)_i x_i\geq\ell\right\}.
\]
For every \(z\in D_{r,t}\), the sum in this definition is at most \(\ell\).  Equality requires \(z_i=(z_t)_i\) for all \(i\in\operatorname{supp}z_t\); since \(z\) already then has \(\ell\) nonzero coordinates and \(D_{r,t}\) permits support at most \(\ell\), all its remaining coordinates must vanish.  Hence \(J_t\cap D_{r,t}=\{z_t\}\).  If \(\ell=0\), the preceding threshold inequalities give \(D_{r,t}=\{0\}\), and the proper closed halfspace \(J_t:=\{x:x_1\geq0\}\) again satisfies \(J_t\cap D_{r,t}=\{z_t\}\).

Apply the defining centerpoint inequality for \(z_t\) to this exposing halfspace.  Since \(w_{r,t}\) vanishes off \(D_{r,t}\),
\[
b^\ell-t=w_{r,t}(z_t)
=\sum_{z\in J_t\cap\mathbb Z^r}w_{r,t}(z)
\geq2^{-r}W_r(t).
\]
Thus
\[
W_r(t)\leq2^r(b^\ell-t)<2^rb^\ell=2^ra_r(z_t).
\]
The maximum in the \((\mathrm{FP})\) ratio is therefore exactly \(2^rb^\ell\), proving
\[
\frac{\max\{W_r(t),2^ra_r(z_t)\}}{T_r}
=\frac{2^rb^\ell}{(1+2b)^r}
\leq\left(\frac2{1+2b}\right)^r.
\]
Because \(b>1/2\), the base \(2/(1+2b)\) is strictly less than \(1\).  Given any proposed universal \(c>0\), choose \(r\) so large that \((2/(1+2b))^r<c\).  Then every pair allowed by the existential quantifiers of \((\mathrm{FP})\) has \(\max\{W_r(t),2^ra_r(z_t)\}<cT_r\).  This negates the asserted universal \(c\), with all threshold and centerpoint choices covered.

It remains to separate this obstruction from the locked target.  Negation preserves \(S_r\) and its mixed-integer measure, because \(C_r=-C_r\) and \(-\mathbb Z^r=\mathbb Z^r\).  Let \(H\) be any closed halfspace containing the origin.  If \(H\) is proper, translating its boundary toward the origin produces a boundary-through-origin halfspace \(H_0\subseteq H\).  The opposite halfspace \(-H_0\) has the same mixed-integer measure as \(H_0\), and \(H_0\cup(-H_0)\) contains all of \(S_r\).  Hence
\[
\mathcal H_r(S_r\cap H)\geq\mathcal H_r(S_r\cap H_0)\geq T_r/2.
\]
The same conclusion is immediate if \(H\) is the whole space.  Conversely, the halfspace \(\{(x,s):s_1\geq0\}\) contains the origin, its boundary has zero \(r\)-dimensional measure in every lattice fiber, and central symmetry gives it mixed-integer measure exactly \(T_r/2\).  Therefore \(h_{S_r}(0)=T_r/2\).

Finally, for any \(y=(z,s)\in S_r\), the two closed halfspaces
\[
\{(x,u):u_1\geq s_1\},
\qquad
\{(x,u):u_1\leq s_1\}
\]
both contain \(y\).  Their common boundary has zero \(r\)-dimensional measure in every lattice fiber, so their mixed-integer measures sum to \(T_r\); at least one is at most \(T_r/2\).  Thus \(h_{S_r}(y)\leq T_r/2\) for every \(y\), while equality holds at the origin.  This proves the claimed optimal normalized depth \(1/2\), and since \(c_0\,2^{-r}<1/2\) for every \(r\geq1\) and \(c_0<1/e\), it also proves that these bodies satisfy rather than refute the locked target.
statement:
Put \(\theta _0:=1-1/e\), and fix any
\[
\frac12<b<\theta _0.
\]
For \((x,s)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\), put \(\rho:=|x|\) and define the full-dimensional centrally symmetric hexagonal convex body
\[
B_b:=\{(x,s):\rho\leq1,\quad 2|s|+(1-b)\rho\leq1\}.
\]
For each \(r\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), after grouping the first and second coordinates of the factors, let
\[
C_r:=B_b^r\subseteq\mathbb R^r\times\mathbb R^r,\qquad
S_r:=C_r\cap(\mathbb Z^r\times\mathbb R^r).
\]
For \(z\in\mathbb Z^r\), let \(a_r(z)\) be the \(r\)-dimensional volume of the fiber \((C_r)_z\), and let \(T_r:=\sum_z a_r(z)\).  Then
\[
a_r(z)=
\begin{cases}
b^{|\operatorname{supp}z|},&z\in\{-1,0,1\}^r,\\
0,&z\notin\{-1,0,1\}^r,
\end{cases}
\qquad
T_r=(1+2b)^r.
\]
For \(t\geq0\), define
\[
w_{r,t}(z):=(a_r(z)-t)_+,\qquad
W_r(t):=\sum_z w_{r,t}(z),\qquad
D_{r,t}:=\{z:w_{r,t}(z)>0\}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal C_{r,t}\) be the weighted lattice centerpoint set from accepted fact `a0f438972c88d08b`: its elements are the lattice points \(z_t\in\operatorname{conv}(D_{r,t})\) for which every proper closed halfspace \(J\subseteq\mathbb R^r\) containing \(z_t\) satisfies
\[
\sum_{z\in J\cap\mathbb Z^r}w_{r,t}(z)\geq2^{-r}W_r(t).
\]
For every \(t\geq0\) with \(W_r(t)>0\) and every \(z_t\in\mathcal C_{r,t}\) satisfying the \((\mathrm{FP})\) feasibility condition
\[
t\geq\theta _0a_r(z_t),
\]
if \(\ell:=|\operatorname{supp}z_t|\), then
\[
W_r(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}2^j\binom rj(b^j-t),
\qquad
\frac{\max\{W_r(t),\,2^ra_r(z_t)\}}{T_r}
=\frac{2^rb^\ell}{(1+2b)^r}
\leq\left(\frac2{1+2b}\right)^r.
\]
Consequently, for every \(c>0\), some \(r\) makes every feasible pair fail
\[
\max\{W_r(t),2^ra_r(z_t)\}\geq cT_r.
\]
Thus the universal assertion \((\mathrm{FP})\) stated in accepted fact `a0f438972c88d08b` is false.

Nevertheless,
\[
h_{S_r}(0)=\frac12T_r
\quad\text{and}\quad
\frac1{T_r}\sup_{y\in S_r}h_{S_r}(y)=\frac12.
\]
In particular, for every \(c_0\in(0,1/e)\), the origin satisfies
\[
h_{S_r}(0)\geq c_0\,2^{-r}T_r,
\]
so this family does not disprove the locked weak Oertel target.
